entities.name: Companion Planting
entities.description: The practice of growing different plants in proximity for mutual benefit, including pest control, pollination support, and improved yield.

hasChunks.text: Companion planting pairs plants that benefit each other — growing basil near tomatoes repels aphids and improves fruit flavour.
Three Sisters planting — corn, beans, and squash grown together — is the classic North American example of companion planting in practice.

entities.name: Crop Yield
entities.description: The measurable amount of agricultural produce harvested per unit area, typically expressed in kilograms per hectare or pounds per acre.

hasChunks.text: Improving crop yield depends on soil quality, water management, pollinator activity, and — increasingly — well-chosen companion plantings.

entities.name: Pest Damage
entities.description: The reduction in plant health or harvestable yield caused by insects, rodents, fungi, or other organisms feeding on or otherwise harming cultivated plants.

hasChunks.text: Pest damage can be significantly reduced through companion planting, encouraging natural predators, and rotating crops between seasons.

entities.name: Acme Gardens
entities.description: An independent horticultural consultancy and online resource publishing guides on companion planting, soil management, and small-scale organic growing, with on-site advisory services across southern France.

hasChunks.text: Acme Gardens is an independent horticultural consultancy founded in 2018, publishing field-tested guides and offering on-site advisory work across southern France.

entities.name: Companion Planting Consultation
entities.description: A paid advisory service in which an Acme Gardens horticulturist surveys a client's plot, identifies pest and yield issues, and produces a season-by-season companion-planting plan tailored to the site's soil, climate, and existing crops.

hasChunks.text: A Companion Planting Consultation includes a two-hour site visit, soil and exposure assessment, and a written planting plan covering the next three growing seasons.
Most clients book a consultation in late winter, giving time to source seed and prepare beds before the spring sowing window.

entities.name: Service Coverage Area
entities.description: The set of cities in which Acme Gardens delivers on-site Companion Planting Consultations. Coverage reflects the area reachable within a single-day round trip from the Marseille office and is reviewed each season.

hasChunks.text: On-site consultations are available in Marseille and Aix-en-Provence. Sites outside this area can be served remotely via photo survey and a video walk-through.

entities.name: Marseille
entities.description: France's second-largest city and the principal port of the Mediterranean coast. Its hot dry summers and limestone soils favour drought-tolerant companions such as rosemary and thyme interplanted with tomatoes and courgettes.

hasChunks.text: Marseille's coastal microclimate — hot summers tempered by the Mistral — rewards aromatic companions that shade the soil and draw pollinators through the dry months.

entities.name: Aix-en-Provence
entities.description: A historic city in the Bouches-du-Rhône department, 30km north of Marseille. Slightly cooler summers and heavier clay soils than the coast make it well-suited to deeper-rooted companions such as artichokes and broad beans.

hasChunks.text: Aix-en-Provence's heavier soils hold spring moisture longer than the coast, extending the window for cool-season companions like broad beans and peas alongside early brassicas.
